here is my code to extract the legend:

g_legend<-function(a.gplot){
  tmp <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(a.gplot))
  leg <- which(sapply(tmp$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
  legend <- tmp$grobs[[leg]]
  return(legend)
}

legend <- g_legend(some_plot)
cairo_pdf("some.pdf",width=??,height=??)

I am struggling since a couple of hours to retrieve the height and width of the legend to replace the "??" with.

I'd appreciate any help or pointers to possible solutions,
thanks -
Peter

You can have several geoms in one ggplot() call, but they should not be nested within each other. Given your code, you have the 4th and 5th line nested under geom_line().

ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    subset(df1, year %in% c(2001:2005)), aes(x=time, y=flow, color='df1') +
      geom_line(subset(df2, year %in%    c(2001:2005)), aes(x=time, y=flow, color='df2') + # nested within geom_line
                  scale_color_manual('', limits=c('df1', 'df2'), values=c('red', 'blue')) # nested within geom_line(geom_line(scale_color_manual))

The correct way of "nesting" is the way I showed in two posts back. If you use a (decent enough) IDE, it should set the correct indentation. Lines starting with the same indent are equivalent, but if one is more indented, it is nested within one of the above calls.

Cheers,
Roman

legend$widths and legend$heights give the width and height of the legend as unit vectors. For each, the elements need to be summed, converted to inches, then the unit needs to be stripped off.

width = grid::convertX(sum(legend$widths), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
height = grid::convertY(sum(legend$heights), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)

cairo_pdf("some.pdf", width = width, height = height)
grid::grid.draw(legend)
dev.off()

library(ggplot2)

myData <- data.frame("xVar" = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256),
                     "yVar" = 1:9)

I have intentionally plotted the original values on a log2-transformed x axis, rather than transform the values themselves so as to preserve some interpretability of the values. To make it more immediately obvious that the x axis is transformed, I would like to set the minor grid line breaks to show the cycles of each decade, as shown here: https://msu.edu/course/fsc/441/6cycle.gif

Is there a way of doing this for both this log2 transformation, and for log10 transformations also?

Hefin

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jatin,

My basic approach would be

load("ALL_HOURLY_NOX_Processed")

data_plot <- max_conc
dimnames(data_plot) <- list(lon = lon, lat = lat)

data_plot <- reshape2::melt(data_plot, value.name <http://value.name> = "max_conc")

ggplot(data_plot, aes(lon, lat, color = max_conc, z = max_conc)) +
  stat_contour(aes(color = ..level.., fill = ..level..), geom =
"contour", bins = 10)

But here we hit a dead end, because stat_contour doesn't generate
lines that work with geom_polygon, and we need geom_polygon for fill.

ggplot(data_plot, aes(lon, lat, color = max_conc, z = max_conc)) +
  stat_contour(aes(color = ..level.., fill = ..level..), geom =
"polygon", bins = 10)

is tantalizingly close, but not good enough. Making it work correctly
will be hard I'm afraid. See
https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/1066 and despair.

Something along the lines of

ggplot(data_plot, aes(lon, lat, z = max_conc)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = max_conc)) +
  geom_contour(bins = 10)

might be good enough.

Best,
Ista

messages.body_plain:
I have some stacked bar charts with stacked text labels produced by geom_bar and geom_text. According to the blog https://blog.rstudio.org/2016/11/14/ggplot2-2-2-0/ the stacking behaviour of geom_bar has been reversed such that the order of items is the same as in the legend. Because geom_text seems not to be changed accordingly, the charts are wrongly formatted now.

Is there a chance to change this? I suggest one of the following:
revert to the old behaviour of geom_bar
add an option to geom_bar to reverse the order (default is behaviour from 2.1.0: reverse = false)
the new geom_col function may use the new ordering (default: reverse = true)
Alternatively a less invasive change would be to reverse the order of the legend.
If 1 - 4 are not an option please change geom_text according to geom_bar

Thank you for your support (and sorry if the post is posted twice)!

Claude

messages.subject: Applying different nls models to different facets/groups using geom_smooth
messages.subject_clean: Applying different nls models to different facets/groups using geom_smooth
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, suppose I have a data frame:

df <- data.frame(Group = c(rep("A", 7), rep("B", 7), rep("C", 7)),
                 Time = c(rep(c(1:7), 3)),
                 Result = c(100, 96.9, 85.1, 62.0, 30.7, 15.2, 9.6,
                            10.2, 14.8, 32.26, 45.85, 56.25, 70.1, 100,
                            100, 55.61, 3.26, -4.77, -7.21, -3.2, -5.6))

and I want to plot the data as Result vs Time, facetting by Group. I want to draw nls models to the plots using geom_smooth which when applying to only one group at a time (A) works well:

ggplot(data = df[df$Group == "A",], aes(x = Time, y = Result)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Group) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "nls", formula = y ~ a+(b-a)/(1+(x/c)^d), se = FALSE,
              method.args = list(start = c(a = -3, b = 85, c = 4, d = 10)))

But the problem I face is that I only understand how to specify one formula, and one set of starting values in the call to geom_smooth, so if I want to draw models with very different formulae or starting values, I can't. For example, here if I try to draw a separate model for each facet/group, it fails on one of the facets:

ggplot(data = df, aes(x = Time, y = Result)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Group) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "nls", formula = y ~ a+(b-a)/(1+(x/c)^d), se = FALSE,
              method.args = list(start = c(a = -3, b = 85, c = 4, d = 10)))

So my question is when applying geom_smooth by a grouping/facetting variable, is there a way to specify separate models? Or is the only option to simply model each in isolation and then use something like gridExtra to panel them together again afterwards?

As an off topic aside, the nls() function is really bad at parameter estimation. There are online widgets which can estimate parameters without any user defined starting values, so why is nls() so far behind? Am I missing something?

Thanks
Hefin

I have a different more brutal approach to a similar problem: facetting
muliple variables (with different units) in ggplot2.

My solution is:

library(devtools)

install_github("oneyb/ggcrap")

library(ggcrap)

library(reshape2)
## simulate a model study
air <- transform(airquality, Ozone.model = Ozone +
rnorm(length(Ozone), 2),
Wind.model = Wind + rnorm(length(Wind)))
## Add time, see ?airquality
air$dtm <- as.Date(paste("1973", air$Month, air$Day,
sep = "-"), format="%Y-%m-%d", tz="EST")
d.f <- melt(air, id.vars = "dtm", measure.vars = c("Wind", "Wind.model",
"Ozone", "Ozone.model"))
d.f$type <- ifelse(grepl("model", d.f$variable), "Modeled", "Measured")
d.f$Variables <- sub("\\.model", "", d.f$variable)
plot <- ggplot(d.f, aes(dtm, value, color=type)) + geom_line()
(box <- plot + facet_grid(Variables~., scales="free_y"))
x11()
(move_facet_strip_y(box))

## Use fancy units
d.f$Variables <- rerevalue(d.f$variable,
c("Wind~'('*m~s^{-1}*')'"="Wind.*", "Ozone~'('*mol~mol^{-1}*')'"="Ozone.*"))
plot <- ggplot(d.f, aes(dtm, value, color=type)) + geom_line()
(box <- plot + facet_grid(Variables~., scales="free_y",
labeller=label_parsed))
x11()
(move_facet_strip_y(box))

I hope that helps. There's more crap in the package, with some examples.

Best,

Brian
